assets.title: Global Sea Surface Currents and Temperature
assets.credit: NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center Scientific Visualization Studio
assets.legend: Flow lines coloured by modelled sea surface temperature: blue 0 C, green 10-20 C, yellow about 25 C, red 32 C. Colorbar file: sst_ecco2_cbar.png
limitations: Model output, not observation.
Flow lines are a rendering; values between model grid points are interpolated.
Equirectangular map: pixel scale varies with latitude.
Covers one modelled year; not a climate trend.

assets.title: Perpetual Ocean 2: Western Boundary Currents
assets.role: rejected as first input; possible context

assets.title: GEOS Aerosols (2025)
assets.role: second source (approved by Dev A, 15 Nov), one still
assets.eic_gallery: Not in the Earth Information Center gallery (checked 2026-11-15). Used as a challenge resource: 'GEOS Aerosols' in the challenge's resource list. Describe it as a challenge resource, not EIC data.
assets.credit: NASA's Global Modeling and Assimilation Office (GMAO) and NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS)
assets.legend: Aerosol type: blue sea salt, pink/magenta dust, orange/red smoke from fires, green sulfates from pollution and volcanoes. Colour bar file: Aerosols_cbar.png

map_geometry.checked: lon/lat grid on the still: 0 line passes the UK and the Ghana coast, 60N meets Greenland's southern tip, Antarctica from about 70S

limitations: Model output (GEOS-FP replay), not an observation.
One moment only (19 Aug 2025 20:00 UTC): no change over time, so each region plays a steady rhythm.
Plumes are a rendering of modelled aerosol; the numbers describe the drawn picture, not air quality or amounts.
Pixels are not square (16:9 world map): 0.094 degrees per pixel east-west, 0.083 north-south.

assets.title: Near Real-Time Global Precipitation from the Global Precipitation Measurement Constellation
assets.role: third source (proposed 15 Nov; for Dev A to approve), 30 hourly frames
assets.eic_gallery: Yes: listed in the Earth Information Center 'Daily Visualizations' dashboard (gallery/daily-visualizations), part of the EIC content.
assets.model_or_instrument: GPM IMERG near real-time (GPM constellation of satellites)
assets.legend: Liquid precipitation rate green (0.1) to yellow (0.5-1) to orange (2-3) to red and dark red (5-50 mm/hour); frozen precipitation cyan to purple (0.1-50 mm/hour). Colour bar files: rainbarwhite2.png, snowbarwhite2.png
downloads_to_use: frames/3600x1800_2x1_30p/flatcomposite/, 30 frames one hour apart, 14 Nov 00:00 to 15 Nov 05:00 UTC, saved and renumbered 0-29 (list: assets/imerg_frames.txt)
assets.rolling_folder: NASA keeps only about the latest 7 days in this folder, so these frames disappear from NASA after about 21 Nov 2026. Keep the saved copy; the download script works only while NASA still has them.

map_geometry.checked: lon/lat grid on frame 0: 0 line passes the UK and Ghana; same layout as SVS 3912

motion_check.method: phase correlation of frame 0 vs frame 29
motion_check.result: shift 0.15 px (a 6 px test shift is measured as 6.00): fixed camera

limitations: Near real-time rain estimates, later replaced by NASA's research-quality version.
Land is a satellite photo, so land is found from the SVS 3912 land outline plus pixels that never change; both circles are open ocean.
A small 'L' mark sits in the bottom-right corner (masked as static).
Rain comes and goes: a circle with no rain in a frame makes that beat missing. Both chosen circles have rain in all 30 frames.
The numbers describe the drawn rain picture, not how much it rains.
